title: If-Else
concept: Add an else branch to handle the 'otherwise' case — do one thing when true, another when false.
why: Most decisions have two outcomes: pass or fail, valid or invalid. If-else captures this binary choice perfectly.
tips: Exactly ONE branch runs — the `if` block or the `else` block
`else` does NOT have its own condition — it catches everything `if` doesn't
Use `if-else` when the two cases are opposites (pass/fail, yes/no)
The `else` must immediately follow the `if` block's closing brace
common_mistakes: Putting a condition after `else`: `else score < 60` is wrong — just `else`
Forgetting braces around the else block
Thinking both blocks can run — they can't; it's one or the other
